situation: A close friend asks how you are after a hard week you have not talked about.
say: I'm fine yaar, all good.
better: Honestly, not great. This week has been heavy. Can I tell you about it?
also: I've been better, to be honest. Got time for a chai?
weak: Fine fine, what to do, life is like this only.
Chhodo, no point discussing.
why: Honest and specific; it opens the door instead of closing it.

situation: Your mother keeps asking about your job search, and it is making you anxious.
say: Mummy, tension mat lo, I'll manage.
better: Ma, I know you worry. Right now the questions make me more anxious. I'll update you every Sunday.
also: I'm stressed about it too. Can we talk once a week instead of every day?
weak: Why you keep asking same thing, I said I'll manage.
Everything is under control, don't worry about me.
why: Names the feeling and offers a plan, so worry has somewhere to go.

situation: Your manager asks if you can handle a new project on top of three others.
say: Yes sir, no problem, I'll manage somehow.
better: I'm stretched thin right now. If I take this on, one of the other three will slip. Which matters most?
also: I'm at capacity. Can we look at my list together and decide what to drop?
weak: Okay, I'll adjust, no issues.
Sir, already I'm dying with work, how can I take more?
why: Says you are overloaded calmly and asks for a decision, not sympathy.

situation: A colleague covered your work when you were ill.
say: Thanks for the help, bro.
better: Thank you for covering for me last week. I could actually rest because of you. I owe you one.
also: I really appreciated you stepping in. It made a big difference.
weak: Thanks, thanks, adjust kar liya na, that's what friends are for.
Ya thanks, I would have done the same.
why: Specific thanks, saying what it changed, means far more than a quick 'thanks'.

situation: You cleared an exam you had failed twice before, and a friend congratulates you.
say: Arre, it was just luck, nothing big.
better: Thank you! I'm really proud of this one. Third attempt, and I worked hard for it.
also: Thanks, I'm so happy. It took a lot to get here.
weak: Paper was easy this time, that's all.
Haan, finally, God knows how it happened.
why: Owning your pride is not boasting; brushing it off hides real effort.

situation: You are sad after a friend moved to another city.
say: It's okay, people come and go, that's life.
better: I miss her more than I expected. The evenings feel empty without our walks.
also: I'm a bit low since she left. I didn't realise how much I relied on her.
weak: I'm totally fine, actually I'm enjoying the free time.
Whatever, she'll forget me anyway.
why: Naming the sadness and its reason helps you, and others, understand it.

situation: Your partner asks why you have been quiet all evening.
say: Nothing. I'm just like that only.
better: Sorry, I'm in my head. Work went badly today and I'm still upset about it.
also: I'm tired and a bit low. It's not about you. Can I tell you after dinner?
weak: You won't understand, leave it.
Kuch nahi, why are you asking so many questions?
why: Explains the mood so the other person does not guess, or blame themselves.

situation: Before an interview, a relative asks if you are nervous.
say: No no, I'm fully confident, cool hai.
better: A little nervous, yes. But I've prepared well, so it's the good kind of nervous.
also: Bit jittery, honestly. That usually means I care about it.
weak: Very very tense, I think I'll mess it up.
Nervous? Me? Never, I don't feel all that.
why: Admitting a little fear is honest and calm; denial or panic are not.

situation: You feel left out because friends planned a trip without you.
say: Cool, enjoy, I anyway didn't want to come.
better: I'll be honest, I felt a bit left out when I saw the trip plan. Was there a reason?
also: It stung a little not to be asked. I'd love to be included next time.
weak: Nice, so now I'm not part of the group, I see.
No problem, I'm used to it.
why: Say the hurt directly instead of hiding it in sarcasm.

situation: A teacher who helped you years ago messages to congratulate you.
say: Thank you ma'am, all because of your blessings.
better: Thank you, ma'am. Your belief in me in Class 10 changed how I saw myself. I still remember it.
also: It means a lot to hear from you. You were the first person who pushed me.
weak: Thanks ma'am, by god's grace.
Thank you ma'am, ok, take care.
why: Gratitude lands when you name exactly what the person did.

situation: Your friend asks how you are after your grandfather's death.
say: I'm okay. He was old, it was bound to happen.
better: I'm sad. I knew it was coming, but I still miss him every day.
also: Some days are fine, some are hard. Thanks for asking.
weak: All okay, no need to discuss.
What to do, everyone has to go one day.
why: Grief does not need a reason or excuse; it is okay to say it plainly.

situation: A friend says 'tension mat lo' when you share a worry, and it does not help.
say: Haan, okay, I won't take tension.
better: I know you mean well. I don't need a fix right now, I just need you to listen for a bit.
also: Thanks. It helps more if you just hear me out.
weak: Easy for you to say, you don't have problems.
Okay fine, forget I said anything.
why: Tells people what kind of support you want, kindly.

situation: You feel overwhelmed planning a sibling's wedding with endless tasks.
say: I'm going mad, everything is on my head only.
better: I'm overwhelmed. I can handle the caterer and guests, but can someone else take the decoration and travel?
also: It's too much for one person. Can we split the list?
weak: Nobody helps in this house, I do everything.
Chalo, I'll do it all, as usual.
why: Names the feeling and asks for specific help, not blame.

situation: You have been feeling low for weeks and decide to tell a close friend.
say: Nothing serious, just thoda mood off.
better: I've been feeling low for a few weeks, and it's not lifting. I wanted someone to know.
also: I've not been myself lately. Can we talk? I might also see a counsellor.
weak: It's just overthinking, I'll be fine by tomorrow.
Don't ask, I'm useless these days.
why: Saying how long and how much lets people take it seriously and help.

situation: Your father did something kind, and your family rarely says such things aloud.
say: Papa, thanks, haan.
better: Papa, I noticed you drove two hours just to drop my books. Thank you. It meant a lot.
also: I don't say it much, but I'm grateful for what you do.
weak: Why you took so much trouble, no need.
Okay, thank you, bye.
why: Plain, specific thanks to family feels awkward once and warm for long.

situation: You feel jealous of a friend's promotion and it is affecting your mood.
say: Good for him, but he's just lucky and smooth-talking.
better: I'm happy for him, and honestly also a bit jealous. I want that kind of growth too.
also: It's made me think about where I'm stuck. That's on me, not him.
weak: Promotions here only go to chamchas.
I'm not jealous at all, why would I be?
why: Admitting envy honestly turns it into useful information about what you want.

situation: Your manager praises your work in a team meeting.
say: No sir, it was nothing, team effort only.
better: Thank you. I'm proud of how it turned out, and Priya's data work made a big difference too.
also: Thanks, I worked hard on it. Glad it helped.
weak: Sir, I just did my duty, nothing special.
Haan, I did most of it actually.
why: Accept praise, then share credit fairly; don't deny or grab it.

situation: You are anxious about results day and a cousin keeps joking about it.
say: Haha, yes yes, I'll fail only.
better: I'm really anxious about results, so the jokes are hard to hear today. Can we skip them?
also: I know you're joking, but I'm tense. Please go easy.
weak: Shut up, you're so irritating.
Haha, good one, very funny.
why: A clear, calm request works better than fake laughter or snapping.

situation: Your friend asks why you cancelled plans again.
say: Something came up, sorry yaar.
better: Honestly, I've been drained and needed a night alone. It's not you. Can we meet Saturday?
also: My social battery is empty this week. I'd still love to see you soon.
weak: Office work, you know how it is.
Some family function, next time pakka.
why: The true reason, said kindly, protects the friendship better than excuses.

situation: A relative asks if you are happy living alone in Bengaluru.
say: Super happy, best decision of my life.
better: Mostly, yes. I love the freedom, though some evenings I do feel lonely.
also: It's a mix. Good for my career, harder on the heart.
weak: Very lonely, I don't know why I came.
What happiness, just surviving.
why: Mixed feelings are normal; saying both sides sounds honest and settled.

situation: You feel embarrassed after a mistake in front of the whole class.
say: I don't care, it doesn't matter to me.
better: That was embarrassing. I froze. I'll laugh about it in a week, but right now it stings.
also: Okay, that wasn't my best moment. I'm a bit embarrassed.
weak: Everyone was laughing at me, I'm never speaking again.
Whatever, they are all idiots.
why: Owning a small embarrassment shrinks it; pretending makes it bigger.

situation: Your spouse planned a surprise birthday dinner for you.
say: Why you wasted so much money?
better: I'm so touched. Nobody has done this for me in years. Thank you.
also: This made my whole week. I feel really loved.
weak: Nice, but you shouldn't have.
Okay, okay, very good.
why: Receive kindness warmly; deflecting it can feel like rejecting the giver.

situation: You are stressed about money and your partner asks what is wrong.
say: Nothing, you won't understand these things.
better: I'm worried about money this month. The EMI and rent hit together. Can we sit and plan it?
also: I'm stressed about our budget. I'd feel better if we looked at it together.
weak: Everything is costly, how will we survive?
It's my headache, don't bother.
why: Names the exact worry and invites teamwork instead of shutting out.

situation: You are relieved after a parent's surgery went well, texting the family group.
say: Surgery done. All ok.
better: Papa's surgery went well. I'm so relieved I could cry. Thank you all for the calls and prayers.
also: Good news: surgery went fine. I can finally breathe again.
weak: Ok done.
Surgery over, now let's see what happens.
why: Sharing the relief lets people share it with you.

situation: A friend asks for advice, but you are too exhausted to help well tonight.
say: Haan bol, I'm free, tell me.
better: I want to help properly, but I'm exhausted tonight. Can we talk tomorrow morning when I'm fresh?
also: I'm running on empty right now. Give me till tomorrow?
weak: Hmm, hmm, okay, then what? Go on.
Not now, I have my own problems.
why: Honest about your limits, while still showing you care.
